md_description: This workflow captures the generation and analysis of data from traditional medicinal plants used in nutraceutical development. Plant material is extracted and fractionated, active compounds are measured by chromatography and spectroscopy, and their antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects are quantified in cellular assays. The resulting chemical identity and bioactivity outputs are integrated into a unified analysis to support standardization of nutraceutical products and health-benefit claims.

traditional_medicinal_plant_material.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic source-material metadata for the harvested medicinal plant tissue: identity, taxonomic/origin descriptors, harvested plant part, and basic provenance/collection context. I excluded extraction, fractionation, analytical, assay, and signal-related fields because those belong to downstream Process, Capture, Signal, or Derivative nodes. I also avoided any experiment or sample identifiers that would be repeated elsewhere, and did not duplicate upstream/downstream operational details already owned by other nodes.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the harvested plant material sample used as the source for extraction; string format example: MPM-001 or herbarium-linked accession code. Record once at the point the material enters the workflow.

Accepted botanical species name of the medicinal plant source, recorded for the harvested tissue before extraction; string example: Curcuma longa. Use the taxonomically resolved name available for the specimen.
Local or common name used for the medicinal plant source at collection time; string example: turmeric, neem, or ginseng. Record as provided by the source or field notes.
Plant tissue harvested for extraction, recorded at sample intake; examples include leaf, root, rhizome, bark, stem, flower, or seed. This describes the source material only, not any later processing.

Geographic collection location of the harvested plant material, captured at sampling; string example: Chiang Mai Province, Thailand or GPS/site descriptor. Use the best available provenance label for the specimen.
Date when the medicinal plant material was harvested or received into the study, recorded at the source-material stage; ISO date example: 2026-08-18.

Herbarium or voucher specimen identifier associated with the plant material, if a voucher was prepared; string format example: HB-2024-017. Include only if available to support taxonomic traceability.

Physical state of the plant material at the time it was entered into the workflow, before extraction; indicates whether the source tissue was processed fresh or dried. This is a sample-property field, not a process parameter.

Storage condition of the harvested plant material before extraction, recorded at receipt or prior to processing; examples include room_temperature_dry, 4_celsius, frozen_-20_celsius, or desiccated. Describe only how the source material was held.

crude_extraction.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the extraction operation itself: solvent system, extraction conditions, material-to-solvent ratio, time, temperature, and a quality indicator of the crude extract. I excluded plant identity/origin fields because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded extract file/measurement outputs because those belong to the downstream crude_plant_extract Entity. I also avoided chromatography, spectroscopy, and assay details because they are outside this process’s semantic territory, and I did not repeat any fields already generated for the plant material node.

md_schema.descr: Primary solvent or solvent mixture used for crude extraction of the plant material, recorded for the extraction operation; string example: methanol, 70% ethanol, water, or methanol:water (80:20).
Extraction approach applied to convert plant material into crude extract, recorded during the process; examples include maceration, sonication, reflux, Soxhlet, or percolation.
Ratio of plant material mass to extraction solvent volume used during crude extraction, measured at setup; typically reported as g:mL, for example 1:10 or 1:20.
Temperature at which the extraction was performed, recorded during the active extraction step; typical range 0-100 Celsius depending on method, example 25.0 or 60.0.
Duration of the extraction step, measured from start to stop of solvent contact or heating; typical range 10-1440 minutes, example 60 or 240.
Mixing or agitation condition applied during extraction, recorded as an operational setting; examples include none, orbital_shaking, stirring, sonication_pulses, or intermittent_mixing.
Number of independent extraction replicates prepared from the same plant material batch, recorded after setup and before downstream fractionation; typical values are 1-10.
Mass yield of crude extract relative to starting dry plant material, calculated at the end of extraction and sample recovery; typical range 0-100 percent, example 8.5.

Brief process-level quality indicator for the crude extract, recorded after recovery and before fractionation; examples include clear, particulate_present, low_yield, or acceptable_for_fractionation. This summarizes extraction success, not downstream chemistry.

crude_plant_extract.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic properties of the crude plant extract as a material object: identity, physical state, concentration/solids, yield context, and storage/provenance attributes. I excluded extraction protocol details because those belong to the upstream crude_extraction Process, and I excluded fractionation or analytical outputs because those belong downstream. I also avoided repeating plant-source identifiers already owned by the original material node.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the crude plant extract sample, assigned when the extract is recovered from the extraction process; string format example: CE-001. Use once to track the extract through downstream fractionation.

Identifier linking this crude extract back to the extraction batch or preparation run; string format example: EXTR-2026-05-A. Use to connect the entity to its parent process without repeating the process parameters.

Observed physical appearance of the crude extract at intake before fractionation; examples include viscous_liquid, semi_solid, dry_residue, or powder. Record the material state, not processing details.
Observed color of the crude extract at the entity stage, before downstream separation; examples include brown, dark_green, yellow_brown, amber, or pale. Capture as a descriptive material property.
Recovered mass of the crude extract, measured after solvent removal and before fractionation; report in milligrams, typically ranging from 1 mg to 100000 mg depending on scale.

Concentration of the crude extract solution if the extract is stored or reconstituted as a liquid before fractionation; units mg/mL, typical range 0.1-100 mg/mL, measured at the entity handling stage.

Qualitative status of residual solvent in the crude extract after recovery and before fractionation; indicates whether the material is solvent-free enough for downstream work. This is an entity property, not a process parameter.
Storage temperature of the crude extract while held before fractionation; units Celsius, typical values such as -80, -20, 4, or room temperature depending on stability needs.
Number of days the crude extract was stored before entering fractionation, measured from recovery to downstream use; typical range 0-3650 days.

fractionation_purification.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the fractionation operation: separation strategy, chromatographic mode, stationary phase, elution conditions, and a process-level output quality indicator. I excluded crude extract intrinsic properties because those belong to the upstream Entity, and I excluded the resulting fraction file/sample properties because those belong to the downstream enriched_compound_fractions Entity. I also avoided repetition of already generated extraction-related fields and kept the scope limited to how the separation was performed.

md_schema.descr: Separation approach used to divide the crude extract into fractions during the process; examples include column_chromatography, flash_chromatography, prep_hplc, tlc, or liquid_liquid_partitioning.
Chromatographic polarity or interaction mode used during fractionation, recorded at setup; examples include normal_phase, reverse_phase, hydrophobic_interaction, ion_exchange, or gel_filtration.
Stationary phase material used for chromatographic fractionation, recorded as the active separation medium; string example: silica_gel, C18, Sephadex LH-20, or alumina.
Mobile phase or solvent system used during fractionation, recorded as the running solvent composition; string example: hexane:ethyl_acetate (90:10) or water:acetonitrile with 0.1% formic acid.

Elution gradient description used during fractionation, measured during the process; examples include isocratic, step_gradient, or linear_gradient with solvent percentages. Use this to describe how the solvent program changed over the separation run.
Time interval used for collecting eluate fractions during the separation run, measured while the process is active; typical range 0.5-30 minutes depending on method.
Total number of fractions collected from the crude extract at the end of the fractionation process; typical values range from 1 to several hundred depending on scale and resolution.
Percentage of starting crude extract mass recovered as collected fractions after the separation process, measured at process completion; typical range 0-100 percent.

Process-level indicator of fractionation success, recorded after run completion and prior to downstream analysis; examples include clean_separation, mixed_fractions, overloaded_column, or acceptable. This summarizes separation performance, not fraction identity.

enriched_compound_fractions.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic properties of the collected fractions: fraction identifier, parent batch linkage, physical amount, appearance, and storage/handling attributes. I excluded chromatographic separation parameters because those belong to the upstream fractionation_purification Process, and I excluded analytical identity or bioactivity results because those belong to downstream capture, signal, and derivative nodes. I also avoided duplicating crude-extract identifiers and kept the fields focused on what a downstream user needs to track and select fractions for analysis and assays.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for an individual compound-enriched fraction, assigned after collection from the fractionation process; string format example: F-001 or FRACTION_A12.

Identifier linking the fraction to its parent fractionation run or collection batch; string format example: FRAC-2026-05-01. Use for traceability from the collected fraction back to the process that produced it.

Ordinal number or label of the collected fraction within the fractionation sequence, assigned at collection; examples include 1, 2, 3, or A1. Record the collector’s fraction index, not the separation settings.
Volume of the collected fraction, measured after collection and before downstream analytics or assays; units mL, typical range 0.1-100 mL depending on the separation scale.
Recovered dry mass or residue mass of the fraction, measured after solvent removal if applicable; units mg, typically ranging from 0.1 mg to 10000 mg.

Observed physical appearance of the fraction at the entity stage; examples include clear_liquid, colored_solution, viscous, oily, or dry_residue. This describes the material state, not a process condition.

Qualitative selection status indicating whether the fraction is prioritized for spectroscopy or cellular assay workflows; record at handoff to downstream analysis. Examples include high, medium, low, or not_selected.
Storage temperature for the fraction while held before analytical or bioassay workflows; units Celsius, typical values such as -80, -20, 4, or room temperature.
Number of days the fraction was stored before being used in downstream analysis or assays; measured from collection to handoff, typically 0-3650 days.

chromatographic_profile_capture.reasoning: This node is a Capture, so I included only the measurement session and instrument configuration: instrument identity, acquisition mode, separation column, source/detector settings, scan range, and run timing/replicates. I excluded sample/fraction properties because those belong to the upstream enriched_compound_fractions Entity, and I excluded file-format, raw data size, and signal-quality metrics because those belong to the downstream chromatogram_raw_signal Entity. I also kept software details out because the node description emphasizes the instrument session rather than downstream processing, and I avoided repeating fields already generated for the fraction entity.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the LC-MS or HPLC instrument used for chromatographic profiling, recorded for the capture session; string example: Agilent, Thermo Fisher, Waters, Shimadzu.
Instrument model name or number used to acquire the chromatographic profile, recorded at the capture session; string example: Q Exactive, 1290 Infinity II, or LCMS-8060.
Instrument serial number for the LC-MS or HPLC system used in the capture session; string example: SN12345678. Record the hardware identifier to support traceability and calibration history.
Data acquisition mode used during chromatographic profiling, recorded on the instrument; examples include full_scan, targeted, dda, or d ia depending on the LC-MS method.
Chromatographic column type and/or chemistry used for the LC separation during capture, recorded as an instrument setting; string example: C18, phenyl-hexyl, 150 mm x 2.1 mm, 1.7 um.
Column temperature during the chromatographic profiling run, measured at the instrument; units Celsius, typically 20-60 depending on method.
Mobile-phase flow rate used during the chromatographic profiling run, recorded at the instrument; units mL/min, typical range 0.05-2.0 mL/min.
Volume of fraction injected into the LC-MS or HPLC system for measurement, recorded at the capture session; units microliters, typically 1-100 uL.
Mass-to-charge scan range configured for the MS detector during capture, recorded as lower and upper m/z limits; string example: 100-1500 m/z.
Total acquisition time for the chromatographic profiling run, measured from injection to run end; units minutes, typical range 1-240 minutes.
Number of technical replicate injections acquired for the same fraction during the capture session; typical values are 1-5.

Instrument-session quality indicator recorded after the profiling run and before raw data export; examples include acceptable, low_signal, retention_shift, or instrument_error. This describes capture performance, not raw file quality.

chromatogram_raw_signal.reasoning: This node is a Signal, so I included only raw data artefact properties: file format, file size, dimensions, acquisition channel count, and technical quality/storage descriptors. I excluded instrument settings and capture-session parameters because those belong to the upstream chromatographic_profile_capture Capture node, and I excluded any processed peak or compound interpretation because those belong downstream to derivative and process nodes. I also avoided repeating fraction identity or sample provenance fields already owned by the upstream Entity nodes.

md_schema.descr: File format of the exported raw chromatographic signal, recorded at data export; string example: mzML, mzXML, vendor_raw, or netCDF.
Size of the raw chromatographic data file, measured after acquisition and export; units bytes, typically ranging from 1000000 to 10000000000 depending on run length and detector type.
Total number of spectra or chromatographic scans contained in the raw signal file, recorded as a technical property of the dataset; typical range 1 to 100000.
Number of detector channels or traces present in the raw chromatographic output, recorded for the raw file; typical examples include 1 for single-trace HPLC or multiple channels for LC-MS.
Dimensions of the exported raw signal matrix, expressed as rows by columns or scan count by feature count; string example: 5000x3 or 12000x2. Record the technical size of the raw artefact.
Storage location of the raw chromatographic file, recorded after acquisition in the data repository or instrument server; string example: s3://bucket/path/file.mzML or /data/run_001.raw.
Integrity checksum for the raw signal file, recorded after export to verify file transfer and storage; string example: md5:abc123... or sha256:... .

Technical quality indicator for the raw signal file, assessed after export and before downstream processing; examples include complete, truncated, corrupted, or acceptable. This flag describes file integrity and acquisition completeness.

chromatogram_processing.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the computational transformation of raw chromatographic data: software identity, algorithm choices, peak-picking/alignment/deconvolution parameters, and a processing quality indicator. I excluded raw file properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded the resulting feature table dimensions or values because those belong to the downstream compound_feature_table Derivative node. I also avoided duplicating any capture-session hardware settings and limited software-related fields to this processing operation as required.

md_schema.descr: Name of the analysis software used for chromatogram processing, recorded for the computational transformation step; string example: MZmine, XCMS, MS-DIAL, OpenMS, or vendor processing suite.
Version of the analysis software used to detect, align, and deconvolute chromatographic features, recorded at run time; string example: 2.53 or 4.1.0.
Software repository or source reference for the chromatogram-processing pipeline, recorded to support reproducibility; string example: GitHub URL, container tag, or package source name.

Peak detection algorithm or strategy used during processing, recorded as the computational method applied to raw chromatographic data; examples include centroiding, wavelet, local_maximum, or matched_filter.
Retention-time alignment method used to harmonize peaks across chromatographic runs, recorded during processing; examples include obiwarp, linear_alignment, dynamic_time_warping, or reference_based.
Method used to separate co-eluting signals into analyzable components during processing, recorded at computation time; examples include correlation_based, model_based, or not_applied.

Intensity or signal-to-noise threshold used for feature detection during chromatogram processing, measured in the software configuration; typical range depends on instrument scale, often expressed as arbitrary units or signal-to-noise ratio.
Retention-time tolerance used for peak alignment and grouping during processing, recorded in minutes; typical range 0.01-1.0 minutes depending on method.

Quality indicator for the processed chromatographic features, assessed after computation and before feature-table export; examples include acceptable, low_alignment, overmerged, underdetected, or noisy. This summarizes processing performance, not downstream biological interpretation.

compound_feature_table.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only computed-result properties of the feature table: table identity, dimensions, feature counts, assignment confidence, and technical output quality. I excluded raw signal properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded processing algorithm settings because those belong to the upstream chromatogram_processing Process node. I also avoided biological identity or assay fields because this derivative summarizes chromatographic features and tentative compound assignments only, not definitive structure or bioactivity results.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the computed compound feature table, assigned after chromatogram processing and before downstream analysis; string format example: FT-001. Use to track the derivative dataset as a reusable analytical object.
Identifier of the raw chromatographic signal file or run used to compute this feature table; string format example: RAW-CHR-001 or a file accession. Record lineage from the upstream signal input.
Total number of chromatographic features detected in the computed table, recorded after processing; typical range 1 to 100000 depending on sample complexity.
Number of features that received a tentative compound assignment or annotation in the computed table, recorded after feature annotation; typically less than or equal to the total feature count.
Number of rows in the exported feature table, measured at output generation; typically equals the number of detected features or feature groups.
Number of columns in the exported feature table, measured at output generation; this reflects the number of variables captured per feature, such as retention time, m/z, and intensity.

Average or summary confidence score for candidate compound assignments in the feature table, computed from the annotation workflow; typical range 0.0-1.0 or 0-100 depending on the scoring system. Record the value used by this workflow.
File or serialization format of the computed feature table, recorded at export; string example: csv, tsv, xlsx, parquet, or json.

Technical quality indicator for the computed table, assessed after export and before downstream reuse; examples include acceptable, sparse, overannotated, or incomplete. This describes the derivative output quality, not the raw input signal.

spectroscopic_structure_capture.reasoning: This node is a Capture, so I included only the spectroscopy measurement session and instrument configuration: hardware identity, acquisition nucleus/mode, key spectral settings, and run conditions. I excluded isolated-compound intrinsic properties because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded file-format and spectral-trace quality fields because those belong to the downstream spectroscopic_raw_signal Signal node. I also kept software-processing fields out because this node is about instrument capture, not interpretation, and I avoided repeating chromatographic capture settings.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the NMR, MS/MS, or related spectroscopy instrument used for structure capture, recorded for the measurement session; string example: Bruker, JEOL, Thermo Fisher, or Waters.
Instrument model used to acquire the raw structural signal, recorded at the capture session; string example: Avance Neo, QTOF, Orbitrap, or similar.
Hardware serial number of the spectroscopy instrument used in the capture session; string example: SN-XYZ12345. Record for instrument traceability and calibration history.
Spectroscopy modality used for structure capture, recorded as the active measurement mode; examples include nmr, msms, ir, uv_vis, or ram an.
Observed nucleus for NMR acquisition when NMR is the selected modality, recorded during capture; examples include 1H, 13C, or 19F. Leave unfilled only if the modality is not NMR.

Operating frequency or analyzer setting used for the spectroscopy capture, measured at the instrument; units MHz for NMR or an appropriate instrument frequency descriptor for the modality. Typical NMR range is 300-1000 MHz.
Number of scans or acquisitions accumulated for the raw structural signal during the capture session; typical range 1 to 100000 depending on sample amount and modality.

Instrument spectral resolution configured for the acquisition session, recorded as a technical setting; units may be Hz, ppm, or m/z depending on modality. Include the modality-specific value used in this workflow.

Temperature at which the spectroscopy measurement was acquired, recorded during the capture session; units Celsius, typical range from cryogenic or room temperature to elevated temperatures depending on method.
Duration of the spectroscopy acquisition session, measured from start to stop of the capture run; units minutes, typical range 1-1440.

Instrument-session quality indicator recorded after acquisition and before raw file export; examples include acceptable, low_signal, instrument_drift, or incomplete_acquisition. This summarizes capture performance, not spectral interpretation.

spectroscopic_raw_signal.reasoning: This node is a Signal, so I included only raw spectral artefact properties: file format, file size, scan/count dimensions, spectral resolution, storage location, and file-integrity/technical quality fields. I excluded spectroscopy instrument settings because those belong to the upstream spectroscopic_structure_capture Capture node, and I excluded any interpreted structure or identity fields because those belong downstream to the spectral_interpretation Process and structural_assignment_table Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating compound or fraction provenance fields already owned upstream.

md_schema.descr: File format of the exported raw spectral trace, recorded at data export; string example: fid, ser, raw, mzML, mzXML, or vendor_raw depending on modality and instrument.
Size of the raw spectral data file, measured after acquisition and export; units bytes, typically ranging from 1000000 to 10000000000 depending on modality and scan count.
Total number of individual spectra, free induction decays, or acquisition segments contained in the raw signal file, recorded as a technical property of the dataset; typical range 1 to 100000.
Number of detector channels or spectral channels present in the raw output, recorded for the raw artefact; typical values include 1 for single-channel NMR and multiple channels for MS/MS workflows.
Dimensions of the exported raw spectral matrix, expressed as rows by columns or acquisition points by channels; string example: 16384x1 or 5000x3. Record the technical size of the raw artefact.
Storage location of the raw spectral file, recorded after acquisition in the repository or instrument server; string example: s3://bucket/path/file.raw or /data/specimen_01.fid.
Integrity checksum for the raw spectral file, recorded after export to verify file transfer and storage; string example: md5:abc123... or sha256:... .

Technical quality indicator for the raw spectral file, assessed after export and before interpretation; examples include complete, truncated, corrupted, or acceptable. This flag describes file integrity and acquisition completeness.

spectral_interpretation.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the interpretation workflow itself: software/expert agent details, assignment rules, key spectral matching parameters, and a process-level confidence/quality indicator. I excluded raw spectral file properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded the resulting structure annotations because those belong to the downstream structural_assignment_table Derivative node. I also avoided repeating capture instrument settings and kept software identity on this process node per the workflow rules.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software used for spectral interpretation, recorded for the computational part of the process; string example: Mnova, ChemDraw, ACD/Labs, Mass Frontier, or vendor annotation suite.
Version of the interpretation software used to assign structural descriptors, recorded at processing time; string example: 14.0.0 or 2024.1.
Software repository, package source, or pipeline reference used for spectral interpretation, recorded to support reproducibility; string example: GitHub URL, container tag, or package name.
Mode of spectral interpretation used in the process, indicating whether assignments were made computationally, manually by an expert, or by a hybrid approach.

Method used to match spectra against reference libraries or known standards, recorded during interpretation; examples include exact_match, similarity_search, fragment_matching, or chemical_shift_assignment.
Name of the spectral reference library or internal standard set used for comparison, recorded during interpretation; string example: NIST, HMDB, in-house library, or Bruker library.
Similarity or confidence threshold used to accept spectral matches during interpretation, measured as a score or percentage depending on the software; typical range 0.0-1.0 or 0-100.
Number of compounds or structural descriptors assigned during the interpretation step, recorded at process completion; typical range 0 to many depending on sample complexity.

Process-level quality indicator for the spectral interpretation output, assessed after assignment and before table export; examples include high_confidence, mixed_confidence, low_confidence, or unresolved. This summarizes interpretation quality, not the final structure table content.

structural_assignment_table.reasoning: I corrected the structural_assignment_table derivative schema by removing fields that collided with already_generated names across the DAG: annotation_confidence_score, table_row_count, and table_column_count. I retained only non-overlapping derivative fields that still describe the computed structural annotation output: table identity, source signal linkage, assigned counts, export format, and a table-specific quality flag. I excluded raw spectral, capture, and interpretation-process details because they belong to other nodes, and I kept the schema flat and node-specific.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the computed structural assignment table, assigned after spectral interpretation and before downstream integration; string format example: ST-001. Use to track the derivative result as a reusable dataset.

Identifier of the raw spectroscopic signal file or run used to compute this structural assignment table; string format example: SPEC-RAW-001 or a file accession. Record lineage from the upstream signal input.
Number of compounds or molecular entities assigned in the structural table, recorded after interpretation; typical range 0 to many depending on sample complexity and spectral quality.

Number of unique structural descriptors or putative structures reported in the computed table, recorded at output generation; this may differ from compound count if multiple annotations map to one entity.
File or serialization format of the computed structural table, recorded at export; string example: csv, tsv, xlsx, parquet, or json.

Technical quality indicator for the computed structure table, assessed after export and before downstream reuse; examples include acceptable, incomplete, ambiguous, or low_confidence. This describes the derivative output quality, not the raw spectral input.

assay_prep_process.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only preparation-operation fields: purification/formulation approach, solvents or buffers used, concentration adjustment, sterility/cleanup steps, and a process-level suitability quality flag. I excluded source fraction identity because that belongs to the upstream enriched_compound_fractions Entity, and I excluded assay readout or bioactivity metrics because those belong to the downstream isolated_compounds_for_assay Entity and later capture/signal/derivative nodes. I also avoided all previously generated field names and the prior collision-prone generic table/annotation fields.

md_schema.descr: Method used to purify or reformulate enriched fractions into isolated compounds suitable for cellular bioactivity testing, recorded during the preparation process; examples include re-purification, solvent_exchange, drying, desalting, or buffer_exchange.

Separation or cleanup strategy applied during assay preparation, recorded as the active operation used to improve compound suitability; examples include preparative_hplc, solid_phase_extraction, liquid_liquid_partitioning, crystallization, or not_applied.
Solvent or vehicle used to reformulate the isolated compound material for downstream cellular assays, recorded at the preparation step; string example: DMSO, ethanol, water, PBS, or DMSO:water (1:9).

Final concentration of the prepared compound formulation after purification or reformulation, measured at the end of the preparation process; units mg/mL, typically 0.001-100 mg/mL depending on assay requirements.
Estimated purity of the prepared compound material after cleanup and before cellular testing, measured or calculated at the end of the process; units percent, typically 0-100.
Indicates whether desalting or similar cleanup was performed during assay preparation to make the compounds suitable for cell-based testing; record at process completion.

Indicates whether sterile filtration was applied during preparation before cellular assays, recorded at process completion; relevant when compounds are prepared in aqueous or cell-compatible vehicles.
Percentage of starting enriched fraction mass recovered after purification or reformulation, measured at the end of the assay preparation process; typical range 0-100 percent.

Process-level indicator of whether the prepared material is suitable for downstream cellular bioactivity testing, assessed after preparation and before handoff; examples include assay_ready, low_purity, precipitated, or unstable. This summarizes preparation success, not biological activity.

isolated_compounds_for_assay.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I kept only intrinsic assay-ready material properties and removed the colliding purity field by substituting a more specific quality descriptor that does not duplicate earlier metadata. I also excluded preparation protocol details because those belong to the upstream process, and excluded bioactivity readouts because those belong downstream to capture/signal/derivative nodes. The remaining fields describe what the isolated compound sample is, how it is labeled, stored, and presented for cellular testing.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the isolated compound or assay-ready compound sample, assigned after preparation and before cellular testing; string format example: AC-001. Use to track the material through bioassay workflows.
Identifier linking the assay-ready compound back to its preparation batch or source fraction; string format example: ASSAY-2026-05-B. Use for lineage without repeating process parameters.
Name or temporary label of the isolated compound prepared for assay; string example: quercetin, compound_12, or isolate_A. Record the identity label available at the assay-preparation stage.
Physical form of the assay-ready compound material at handoff to bioactivity assays; examples include powder, film, solution, or lyophilized_solid.
Concentration of the assay-ready compound in the testing vehicle or stock solution, measured at handoff to cellular assays; units mg/mL, typically 0.001-100 mg/mL.
Vehicle or solvent used to maintain the isolated compound before or during assay setup; string example: DMSO, water, PBS, or ethanol.

Qualitative status of the isolated compound identity at the assay-ready stage; indicates whether the material is fully identified, tentatively identified, or still provisional before cellular testing.
Storage temperature of the assay-ready compound before cellular testing; units Celsius, typical values such as -80, -20, 4, or room temperature.
Number of days the assay-ready compound was stored before being used in cellular assays; measured from preparation completion to assay start, typically 0-3650 days.

cellular_antioxidant_assay_capture.reasoning: This node is a Capture, so I included only the antioxidant assay measurement session and instrument configuration: hardware identity, detection modality, plate format, readout settings, incubation timing, and capture quality. I removed the duplicated technical_replicate_count field because it already exists in a previous DAG step, and I excluded any compound identity, raw signal, or bioactivity interpretation fields because they belong to upstream Entity, downstream Signal, or later Process/Derivative nodes. The resulting fields stay within the capture node’s territory and avoid cross-step collisions.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the plate reader or imaging system used for the cellular antioxidant assay capture, recorded for the measurement session; string example: BioTek, Molecular Devices, Agilent, or Thermo Fisher.
Instrument model used to acquire the antioxidant assay readout, recorded at the capture session; string example: Synergy H1, SpectraMax iD5, or IncuCyte S3.
Hardware serial number of the plate reader or imaging system used in the antioxidant assay capture; string example: SN-12345678. Record for instrument traceability and maintenance history.
Detection mode used to measure the antioxidant response, recorded during capture; examples include fluorescence, luminescence, absorbance, or imaging.
Microplate format used for the assay capture, recorded at the instrument setup; examples include 6_well, 12_well, 24_well, 48_well, 96_well, or 384_well.
Excitation or emission wavelength configured for the antioxidant assay capture when applicable, recorded at the instrument; units nm, typical range 200-800 nm depending on the assay chemistry.
Signal integration or exposure time used by the instrument during readout acquisition, measured at capture; units milliseconds, typical range 1-10000 ms.
Time between compound treatment and measurement of the antioxidant response, recorded at the assay capture session; units hours, typical range 0.5-168 hours depending on the assay design.

Instrument-session quality indicator recorded after acquisition and before raw data export; examples include acceptable, low_signal, saturated_signal, focus_issue, or instrument_error. This describes capture performance, not biological interpretation.

antioxidant_response_signal.reasoning: This node is a Signal, so I included only raw assay artefact properties: file format, file size, plate/image dimensions, channel count, storage location, and technical quality/integrity flags. I excluded assay instrument settings because those belong to the upstream cellular_antioxidant_assay_capture Capture node, and I excluded normalized responses, IC50 values, or biological interpretation because those belong downstream to bioactivity_quantification and bioactivity_metrics. I also avoided repeating compound identity and assay design fields already owned by upstream entity and capture nodes.

md_schema.descr: File format of the exported raw antioxidant assay readout, recorded at data export; string example: csv, tsv, xlsx, csv.gz, mif, or vendor_raw depending on the assay platform.
Size of the raw antioxidant assay file, measured after acquisition and export; units bytes, typically ranging from 1000 to 1000000000 depending on plate count and image content.
Total number of wells or assay positions represented in the raw signal file, recorded as a technical property of the dataset; typical range 1 to several thousand depending on plate layout.
Number of detection channels present in the raw assay output, recorded for the raw artefact; typical values include 1 for single-signal assays or multiple channels for multiplex readouts.
Dimensions of the exported raw assay matrix, expressed as rows by columns or wells by measurements; string example: 96x3 or 384x5. Record the technical size of the raw artefact.
Storage location of the raw antioxidant assay file, recorded after acquisition in the repository or instrument server; string example: s3://bucket/path/plate001.csv or /data/assay/run_01.
Integrity checksum for the raw antioxidant assay file, recorded after export to verify file transfer and storage; string example: md5:abc123... or sha256:... .

Technical quality indicator for the raw antioxidant assay file, assessed after export and before quantification; examples include complete, truncated, corrupted, or acceptable. This flag describes file integrity and acquisition completeness.

antiinflammatory_assay_capture.reasoning: This node is a Capture, so I included only the measurement session and instrument configuration for the anti-inflammatory assay readout: instrument identity, detection modality, plate format, readout settings, incubation timing, and a session quality flag. I excluded compound identity and formulation fields because those belong to the upstream isolated_compounds_for_assay Entity, and I excluded raw file format or signal-size fields because those belong to the downstream antiinflammatory_response_signal Signal node. I also avoided assay interpretation or potency fields because those belong later to bioactivity_quantification and bioactivity_metrics, and I did not repeat fields already generated for the antioxidant capture step.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the plate reader or imaging system used for the cellular anti-inflammatory assay capture, recorded for the measurement session; string example: BioTek, Molecular Devices, Agilent, or Thermo Fisher.
Instrument model used to acquire the anti-inflammatory assay readout, recorded at the capture session; string example: Synergy H1, SpectraMax iD5, or IncuCyte S3.
Hardware serial number of the plate reader or imaging system used in the anti-inflammatory assay capture; string example: SN-12345678. Record for instrument traceability and maintenance history.
Detection mode used to measure the inflammatory response, recorded during capture; examples include fluorescence, luminescence, absorbance, or imaging.
Microplate format used for the assay capture, recorded at the instrument setup; examples include 6_well, 12_well, 24_well, 48_well, 96_well, or 384_well.
Excitation or emission wavelength configured for the anti-inflammatory assay capture when applicable, recorded at the instrument; units nm, typical range 200-800 nm depending on the assay chemistry.
Signal integration or exposure time used by the instrument during readout acquisition, measured at capture; units milliseconds, typical range 1-10000 ms.
Time between compound treatment and measurement of the inflammatory response, recorded at the assay capture session; units hours, typical range 0.5-168 hours depending on the assay design.

Instrument-session quality indicator recorded after acquisition and before raw data export; examples include acceptable, low_signal, saturated_signal, focus_issue, or instrument_error. This describes capture performance, not biological interpretation.

antiinflammatory_response_signal.reasoning: This node is a Signal, so I included only raw assay artefact properties: file format, file size, plate/image dimensions, channel count, storage location, and technical quality/integrity flags. I excluded assay instrument settings because those belong to the upstream antiinflammatory_assay_capture Capture node, and I excluded normalized responses, fold-changes, or potency estimates because those belong downstream to bioactivity_quantification and bioactivity_metrics. I also avoided repeating compound identity and assay design fields already owned by upstream entity and capture nodes.

md_schema.descr: File format of the exported raw anti-inflammatory assay readout, recorded at data export; string example: csv, tsv, xlsx, csv.gz, mif, or vendor_raw depending on the assay platform.
Size of the raw anti-inflammatory assay file, measured after acquisition and export; units bytes, typically ranging from 1000 to 1000000000 depending on plate count and image content.
Total number of wells or assay positions represented in the raw signal file, recorded as a technical property of the dataset; typical range 1 to several thousand depending on plate layout.
Number of detection channels present in the raw assay output, recorded for the raw artefact; typical values include 1 for single-signal assays or multiple channels for multiplex readouts.
Dimensions of the exported raw assay matrix, expressed as rows by columns or wells by measurements; string example: 96x3 or 384x5. Record the technical size of the raw artefact.
Storage location of the raw anti-inflammatory assay file, recorded after acquisition in the repository or instrument server; string example: s3://bucket/path/plate001.csv or /data/assay/run_01.
Integrity checksum for the raw anti-inflammatory assay file, recorded after export to verify file transfer and storage; string example: md5:abc123... or sha256:... .

Technical quality indicator for the raw anti-inflammatory assay file, assessed after export and before quantification; examples include complete, truncated, corrupted, or acceptable. This flag describes file integrity and acquisition completeness.

bioactivity_quantification.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the computational quantification step: analysis software identity, normalization approach, curve-fitting model, reference controls, potency-summary parameters, and a process-level output quality flag. I excluded raw assay file properties because those belong to the upstream Signal nodes, and I excluded final potency values or table outputs because those belong to the downstream bioactivity_metrics Derivative node. I also avoided repeating instrument/session details from the capture nodes and kept software metadata on this process node per the workflow rules.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software used to normalize cellular readouts and fit dose-response curves, recorded for the quantification process; string example: GraphPad Prism, R, Python, or custom pipeline name.
Version of the software or pipeline used for bioactivity quantification, recorded at processing time; string example: 9.5.1 or 2.1.0.
Software repository, package source, or pipeline reference used for bioactivity quantification, recorded to support reproducibility; string example: GitHub URL, container tag, or package name.

Method used to normalize raw cellular assay readouts before potency estimation, recorded during the quantification process; examples include percent_control, background_subtraction, z_score, or blank_normalization.

Model used to fit dose-response or concentration-response relationships, recorded at processing time; examples include four_parameter_logistic, five_parameter_logistic, linear_fit, or nonparametric_fit.
Type of control used as the assay reference during normalization, recorded for the quantification process; examples include vehicle_control, positive_control, negative_control, or untreated_control.
Number of concentration points used in the fitted dose-response analysis for a compound or condition, recorded during quantification; typical range 2-20 points.

Decision threshold used to accept potency estimates or classify active compounds during bioactivity quantification, recorded in the software configuration; typical range depends on the metric, such as p-value, fold-change, or percent inhibition.

Quality indicator for the quantification output, assessed after normalization and curve fitting and before derivative export; examples include acceptable, poor_fit, insufficient_points, or high_variance. This summarizes processing performance, not final potency values.

bioactivity_metrics.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only computed potency-result properties: metric identifiers, source signal linkage, antioxidant/anti-inflammatory potency summaries, curve-fit outputs, export format, and output quality. I excluded raw assay readout properties because those belong to the upstream Signal nodes, and I excluded the quantification software and fitting parameters because those belong to the upstream bioactivity_quantification Process node. I also avoided collision with prior generic table fields by using bioactivity-specific names and kept the fields focused on the final computed activity metrics only.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the computed bioactivity metrics table, assigned after quantification and before downstream integration; string format example: BM-001. Use to track the derivative result as a reusable dataset.

Identifier of the raw antioxidant assay signal file or run used to compute the antioxidant potency metrics; string format example: ANTIOX-RAW-001 or a file accession. Record lineage from the upstream signal input.

Identifier of the raw anti-inflammatory assay signal file or run used to compute the anti-inflammatory potency metrics; string format example: ANTIINFLAM-RAW-001 or a file accession. Record lineage from the upstream signal input.

Computed antioxidant potency metric derived from the cellular assay signal, recorded after normalization and curve fitting; units depend on the assay and may be percent inhibition, IC50, EC50, or fold-change. Provide the value used in this workflow.

Computed anti-inflammatory potency metric derived from the cellular assay signal, recorded after normalization and curve fitting; units depend on the assay and may be percent inhibition, IC50, EC50, or fold-change. Provide the value used in this workflow.
Unit or reporting basis for the computed potency values, recorded alongside the quantitative result; examples include percent_inhibition, uM, nM, IC50, EC50, or fold_change.

Summary quality indicator for the fitted potency estimates, assessed after quantification and before export; examples include acceptable, poor_fit, insufficient_points, or high_variance. This describes the derivative calculation quality, not the raw assay file.
File or serialization format of the computed bioactivity metrics output, recorded at export; string example: csv, tsv, xlsx, parquet, or json.

Technical quality indicator for the computed bioactivity metrics output, assessed after export and before downstream integration; examples include acceptable, incomplete, inconsistent, or low_confidence.

integrated_nutraceutical_analysis.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the integration operation: analysis software identity, version, repository, merge strategy, cross-domain matching criteria, and a process-level integration quality flag. I excluded source-table properties because those belong to the upstream compound_feature_table, structural_assignment_table, and bioactivity_metrics Derivative nodes, and I excluded the final standardized profile output because that belongs to the downstream standardized_compound_profile Derivative node. I also avoided collision-prone generic table/count fields already generated elsewhere and kept software metadata on this process node per the workflow rules.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or pipeline used to merge compound identity, structure, and bioactivity outputs, recorded for the integration process; string example: Python, R, KNIME, or custom workflow name.
Version of the integration software or pipeline, recorded at processing time; string example: 1.2.0 or 2024.1.

Software repository, package source, or pipeline reference used for the nutraceutical integration step, recorded to support reproducibility; string example: GitHub URL, container tag, or package name.

Strategy used to match compound identity, structure, and bioactivity records during integration, recorded for the process; examples include exact_id_join, name_based_join, structure_based_join, or manual_curation.

Rule used to combine confidence values or evidence across identity, structure, and bioactivity sources during integration, recorded at processing time; examples include minimum, weighted_average, majority_vote, or expert_override.

Number of upstream result sources merged into the integrated nutraceutical analysis, recorded at process completion; typically 2 or 3 for this workflow, corresponding to chemistry and bioactivity evidence streams.
Threshold used to flag cross-source agreement during integration, measured as a score, percentage, or distance depending on the pipeline; typical range 0.0-1.0 or 0-100.

Process-level indicator of the integration outcome, assessed after merging upstream results and before derivative export; examples include acceptable, partial_merge, conflicting_annotations, or unresolved. This summarizes integration performance, not the final profile content.

standardized_compound_profile.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only computed final-profile properties: profile identifier, lineage references to the contributing derivative tables, consolidated identity/structure/bioactivity summary fields, standardization status, export format, and profile quality. I excluded raw assay, capture, and processing parameters because those belong upstream, and I avoided reusing generic table/count fields that caused collisions earlier. I also kept the schema focused on the final integrated nutraceutical-ready output rather than the upstream evidence sources.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the standardized compound profile, assigned after integrated analysis and before downstream use in product standardization or claim support; string format example: CP-001.
Identifier of the compound feature table used as an input to the integrated profile, recorded for lineage and traceability; string format example: FT-001 or upstream accession.
Identifier of the structural assignment table used as an input to the integrated profile, recorded for lineage and traceability; string format example: ST-001 or upstream accession.
Identifier of the bioactivity metrics table used as an input to the integrated profile, recorded for lineage and traceability; string format example: BM-001 or upstream accession.
Concise summary of the compound identity incorporated into the standardized profile, such as accepted name, tentative annotation, or chemotype label, recorded after integration.
Concise summary of the assigned structural information in the standardized profile, such as molecular class, confirmed structure, or tentative structural descriptor, recorded after integration.

Concise summary of the integrated antioxidant and anti-inflammatory bioactivity evidence in the standardized profile, recorded after integration; examples include active, moderately_active, inactive, or mixed_profile.

Status indicating whether the compound profile meets criteria for nutraceutical standardization or claim support, recorded at the final integration stage; examples include standardizable, needs_review, insufficient_evidence, or approved_for_profile.
Qualitative level of support the integrated profile provides for health-benefit or product-claim evaluation, recorded after the final analysis; examples include strong, moderate, weak, or none.
File or serialization format of the standardized compound profile, recorded at export; string example: csv, tsv, xlsx, parquet, or json.

Technical quality indicator for the final standardized profile, assessed after export and before downstream reuse; examples include acceptable, incomplete, conflicting, or low_confidence. This describes the derivative output quality, not the upstream evidence tables.
